title: Runtime tree accounts for all wall time
body:
The -s runtime tree has two branches, seeding and alignment, and neither the top level nor the seeding branch sums to its wall. Query indexing, target indexing and build_pipeline are untimed or printed and discarded. The mmseqs db writes and the prog-mode bookkeeping fall into seeding's [misc.]. The alignment leaves print thread-second sums that read as a bug beside the branch wall.

Done when every branch's leaves plus [misc.] sum to the branch wall, runtime equals the sum of its branches, and the alignment leaves show derived wall time.

Format, settled 2026-09-28: the tree stays. Extra data points go in square brackets. Only the alignment branch gets a column header, with a dashed rule, carried on the tree rail. No new output file, no event log, no timestamps. The target tree is in the notes.

Behavior does not change apart from build_pipeline moving ahead of seed(). The progress println!s in search.rs stay as user feedback.

Open: --stats-results-path (args.rs:421) is validated at args.rs:161 and never written. Either wire it to write the same tree to a file or remove it.
